idiom_name: MikroORM UnitOfWork with FlushMode.COMMIT (em.flush at the transaction end)
implementation_notes: Node has no language-level persistence context, but MikroORM provides one: the UnitOfWork keeps an identity map plus a snapshot of original property values, computes change sets on em.flush(), and runs them inside one database transaction; with FlushMode.COMMIT the flush 'delays ... until the current Transaction is committed', which is the write-behind discipline applied by em.persist() marking and em.flush() writing. What replaces the classic structure: the ORM's unit of work instead of a hand-written dirty map; Sequelize and Prisma write through immediately, so with those the buffer is yours. The hand-rolled version is justified only when batching must span requests.
pitfalls: A forked EntityManager is a unit of work: reusing it across requests leaks the identity map and serves stale entities.
Only managed entities are tracked - plain objects must be persisted explicitly or their changes never reach the flush.
FlushMode.AUTO triggers implicit flushes before overlapping queries; move to COMMIT deliberately and accept unspecified results on non-overlapping reads.
